# 1.2.117 - two accused at the verdict, a project's scene found from its proposer's token, a project's action after the clock is set back, a player's first asks on Foundry 14.370, and what a console always sees

One stage ships: E117, the owner's asks of 16.11.2026 built in this release (the verdict with two accused, a project's
scene found from its proposer's token, a completed project's action after the clock is set back with the reason a GM
sees, and the Debug log's dropped count), line L1's fix of a player's first asks at load on Foundry 14.370, Daggerheart
2.12.9 and a fix to the character sheet. Four lines merged into the assembly: C1 (work toward E40), C4 (work toward
E43), C3 (the player handbook's facts) and L1 (the first run on the owner's own Foundry 14.370 sandbox). **E39, E40,
E43, E53, E58 and E83 are not shipped** and move to 1.2.118 (tools/stages.json): the E40 and E43 work built here ships
as work, not as those stages, whose plans still have parts open (Known gaps); what of E39 and E58 is in, below, is
readings and fixes. E26 stays 1.3.0. From ff3e12e5 (main at 1.2.116, the merge of #66, tag v1.2.116) to aa697521: 31
commits, 4 of them merges of the lines into the assembly (`git rev-list --count` and `--merges --count` over
ff3e12e5..aa697521); the character sheet's fix and this release commit come on top.

In plain words:

**Two accused at the verdict** (E117, built on the E40 line; the owner, 16.11.2026: "gm wybiera czy chce zabic 1, czy 2
i ktora").
- When the count accuses two or more students and at least two of them are alive, the verdict window shows a tick for
  each living accused in place of the "executed" list, each ticked unless the register names them a Blackened
  (verdict.mjs `accusedChoices`).
- If the class got it wrong, exactly the ticked ones are executed: leave both, or untick one to spare them
  (`executedChoice`). With none ticked, **They got it wrong** is greyed out; a verdict sent that way anyway is not
  given, and the GM is told to tick one (`verdictAnswer`). A right verdict ignores the ticks.
- With one accused, or only one of them alive, the window keeps its list, as before. English and Polish, and the GM
  handbook's Verdict section.

**A project stands on the scene of its proposer's token** (E117, built on the E43 line; the owner, 16.11.2026: "co do
projektow to opcja B", and "Tak. Scena niech automatycznie sie wykrywa po tokenie gracza").
- A proposed project stands on the scene its proposer's token stood on, when that scene has the project's room, and
  finds it again from that token when its room changes (projects.mjs `detectedSceneFor`, `proposerSceneFor`).
- Where more than one scene has a room of that name, the project's editor shows **Scene of the room**. A GM's change
  there is a pick that stays through later room changes, and so is a GM dragging the project's token into such a room.
- A world where no two scenes share a room name reads as before (held by a test).
- If the picked scene is deleted or no longer has the room, the editor says so and the project stands where it would
  with no pick, until a GM picks again or that scene holds the room again. When a GM deletes such a scene (only a GM
  can, the owner: "Tylko gm moze to zrobic"), the other GMs get one card naming each project and where it stands now;
  the GM who deleted it gets none.
- A secret project's picked scene stays with the GMs and those in on it: none of a bystander's project rows, world
  settings or copies holds it (scenario 99).

**A completed project's action after the clock is set back** (E117, built on the E43 line; the owner's probe of
16.11.2026 on their world, and their answers "tak" and "b").
- The owner's report from 1.2.114, a completed project's action missing from Facilities, is explained: the project was
  completed on day 3 in the morning, then the clock was set back to day 1, so the action did not stand and nothing said
  why.
- The Projects window and the project's editor now tell a GM why an action does not stand: its time ended (and at which
  time of day), it ended with its chapter or its season, or the clock is earlier than its completion
  (`DRPG.Facility.notLive.*`, English and Polish). Players still see only an action that stands.
- Setting the clock back before a completion now counts as completing the project now: the primary GM's browser writes
  the new time on the project, so its action's lifetime runs from there (facilities.mjs `restampSetBack`). Uses already
  made still count (the owner). The GM handbook's 11.1 says so.

**A player's first asks at load, on Foundry 14.370** (E117; found on the owner's 14.370 sandbox by line L1, 16.11.2026;
14.370 is the one v14 build read, 14.364 and 14.365 were not).
- Four parts of the module asked for a player's own data while Foundry 14.370 had no user yet, and failed on every
  browser, every load: the lock-pick passes, the room actions' uses, the eavesdrops and the timed effects. After a load,
  a player's browser held none of those until the next change sent them, and each browser's session log held "Could not
  register ..." four times. Each ask now waits until the world is ready.
- Measured on the sandbox after the fix: no such failure on the GM or a player, and the GM's browser heard all four asks
  at a player's start.
- `game.drpg.runTests({ tier: 2 })` would have stopped on 14.370 before its first test: two readers of Foundry's
  collections expected a shape 14.370 does not have. Both fixed.

**What a player with a console always sees** (work toward E43; on the owner's consent of 16.11.2026).
- README.md has a new chapter after its Privacy paragraph: what Foundry sends every browser whatever the screen draws
  (every token with its name, place and flags; regions and walls; every sheet and item; every chat message; the trial's
  list of the dead), and what stays with the GMs and the people it concerns.
- The Privacy paragraph's sentence on the GM's Key Remnant plan and a murder declared in the dark is replaced by one
  measured on the harness (on the owner's "oba tak"): where the Remnants lie, the Key Remnants among them, and every
  token's moves in an Eclipse reach every browser; the Key Remnant plan and the declaration do not.

## Before installing

- **No world migration.** No setting is added or removed (`game.settings.register` on 202 lines of scripts/ at both
  ends). The GMs' stores and the player copies keep their definitions (gm-stores.mjs and gm-store.mjs have no change).
- **Projects** gain two stored fields, `roomScene` and `roomSceneByGm` (on the project, or on the GMs' row while it is
  secret). A project saved before this release has neither and stands where it stood.
- **A completed project whose completion is later than the clock** is restamped to now by the primary GM's browser at
  its load (and at every change of the clock's day or time of day), in the same season and chapter only: its action
  stands from then for its lifetime.
- **Language**: lang/en.json goes from 6356 to 6370 keys: 14 added, none removed, none changed in wording (counted on
  the flattened files, ff3e12e5 against a8244e32 and aa697521). lang/pl.json goes from 7441 to 7457: every English key
  and no other but the Polish plural forms (.few, .many; 534, 2 new for the Debug log's count) and the 553 DRPG.Config.*
  keys (same count).
- No icon is added. No console name changed (tools/api-surface.json has no change in the range).
- **Daggerheart**: `verified` goes from 2.12.8 to 2.12.9 (aa697521). This departs from release rule 6, which names in
  `verified` only a version the suite has passed on at a real table: it is the owner's decision (16.11.2026, "3. tak"),
  given after being told that no full gate ran on 2.12.9. 2.12.9 is the version on L1's sandbox, which served 1.2.116
  with L1's commits, not this release's code; the one flow there with real dice was 1.2.116's murder opening. None of
  this release's own changes ran there, the suite's tier 2 did not run there (its 3301 passed is headless, on the
  harness's 2.12.8), and the local gate has not run on it. The README's row and the GM handbook's, English and Polish,
  with it. Of the harness's copies of Daggerheart, one file changed between the two tags (data/action/move-context.mjs,
  one line) and was copied again byte for byte.
- **Foundry**: module.json's compatibility has no change in the range (minimum 14.364, verified 14.365); the sandbox ran
  14.370, which module.json does not name.

## Known gaps

- **Not shipped**: E39, E40, E43, E53, E58 and E83 (tools/stages.json, planned 1.2.118); E83 had no work in this range.
  E26 stays 1.3.0.
- **E40's plan, open parts of its "Done when"**: the 12-rule mutation run is recorded (12 of 12 killed,
  docs/dev/e40/STATUS.md) but is in no gate, and no mutation runner is in the repository; settle() to until() is built
  with no time recorded before and after; the flows `class-trial` and `mastermind` stay partial until E40
  (scripts/tests-flows.mjs).
- **E43's plan, open parts of its "Done when"**: the canary, the fuzz and the matrix are green in the ci layer only (the
  fuzz read once on 14.370 outside the gate, LIVE-E43-01; the local gate has not run, and the matrix never ran on v14);
  the canary plants no closingClaims, diveSets, claimTicket or `passage*` keys; scenarios 31-fuzz and 32-case-security
  are planned for E43 in audit/harness/README.md, and neither file exists.
- **The veiled killer's vision on v14, an open defect** (LIVE-E112-01, measured on 14.370 with token vision on): while
  the opening waits, the killer's own browser still draws their token, but Foundry gives a hidden token no vision, so
  the killer sees from the victim's token instead. Two fixes are proposed in docs/dev/e58/LOCAL-REPORT.md, neither
  built; a fix is planned for 1.2.118.
- **Read at the sandbox and left, each with a default**: a character's name with HTML in it is drawn as HTML in a GM's
  notice (v14 strips scripts and handlers; an image in a name makes the GM's browser load its address); a GM whose
  socket was closed and opened again from the console, without a reload, held stale data (Foundry's; a real network loss
  not read); the victim's chat shows Foundry's "GM privately rolled some dice" at the opening (Foundry's own private
  roll); the gate's Chromium 141 is older than the 146 Foundry 14.370 asks for, and every page shows Foundry's error
  notice. Daggerheart 2.12.9's own code still calls `_del()`, which throws on v14, and its chat card throws on a message
  whose author was deleted (read, not the module's).
- **Found and not fixed**: a race in the harness's fuzz (lib/fuzz.mjs), whose clean-up can read a flag clear before its
  last write lands.
- **Defaults taken, each to confirm**: a GM dragging a project's token into a room several scenes hold picks that scene;
  a stale pick falls back to the rule with no pick and says so, and stands again if its scene holds the room again; the
  proposer's scene is stored even where one scene holds the room, so a scene added later with a room of that name finds
  the project where its proposer stood.
- **Carried from 1.2.116, not closed**: a killer behind a "?" keeps their token's actor (known leak
  `foundry-masked-token-actor`), and a veiled killer's tokens can be told apart from a console
  (`foundry-veiled-token-actor`); 72-canary's three expected reds (`foundry-hidden-tokens`, `foundry-actor-items`,
  `S17-64`).
- **Closed from 1.2.116's list**: the facts files quoting the old Infiltrate order; 18-trial's duplicates, preselection,
  D4's offer applied once and a death before and after discovery; the Calls' phase gates, the Monocub's locks, the
  handover and a proposal's gate now on the shared rule.
